about: The mutant runner shares the capped-child classifier with proclimit.

mutants.name: mut-alias-not-canonical
mutants.rule: An alias and its directory name schedule the same test once.

mutants.name: mut-ambiguous-alias-taken
mutants.rule: A legacy alias that is also a directory with tests names both choices and is refused.

mutants.name: mut-migration-skips-anchors
mutants.rule: The legacy migration includes the test IDs in anchors.

mutants.name: gcoom-mutants-text-only
mutants.rule: A capped mutant child's span-queue allocation fault has reason memory.

mutants.name: fk7a-format-ignored
mutants.rule: A mutated source the formatter would rewrite is invalid, never killed: the runner's format check fails it whatever its edit means.

mutants.name: fk12a-refusal-ignored
mutants.rule: A mutated source the compiler refuses with a new diagnostic is invalid, never killed.

mutants.name: fk12a-declared-ignored
mutants.rule: A row that declares the refusal its point (refused) is judged by its tests: the refusal may kill it.

mutants.name: mutclean-copy-without-git
mutants.rule: The runner's copy carries the checkout's Git file list, so a test that reads the repository (git ls-files) can kill a mutant.

mutants.name: mutants-copy-maintenance-on
mutants.rule: The runner's copy is a Git repository whose own configuration turns automatic gc and maintenance off, so no git run in it starts a repack.

mutants.name: mutclean-other-package-killer-dropped

mutants.rule: A killer in another package of the module (DIR or DIR[TAGS]) is a suite the runner runs, so no row is run by hand.

mutants.name: mutclean-ergo-suite-killer-dropped
mutants.rule: A package ledger's killer named by an ergo suite (lower, std, examples) runs in that suite, with its tools.

mutants.name: mutclean-work-shared
mutants.rule: The default -work is a directory of one run: two runs at once never share coverage counters.

mutants.name: mutclean-work-kept
mutants.rule: The default -work is removed at the end of its run.

mutants.rule: A Go test binary runs with a -test.timeout, as under go test, so a test that bounds its children by t.Deadline judges mutants.

mutants.name: st0-ergo-dir-is-go
mutants.rule: A killer DIR:Name whose DIR is an Ergo package with no Go test is its Ergo test, run by scripts/ergotests (ST-0).

mutants.name: st0-ergo-test-unchecked

mutants.name: lawkiller-law-undeclared
mutants.rule: A killer law:L names a law its package declares; it is refused otherwise, and accepted when declared.

mutants.name: lawkiller-provider-law-unresolved
mutants.rule: A killer DIR:law:pkg.T.L, a member law of the operation type that DIR's package imports as pkg, which DIR's providers run, resolves to the law the imported package declares; a law no imported package declares is refused.

mutants.name: mutmod-nested-cache-shared
mutants.rule: A test of a nested module's suite gets an emission cache of its own (ERGO_CACHE under the work directory): with none, the ergo it starts refuses the user's cache and every hosts/mygo test fails on the unmutated tree.

mutants.name: regen-output-kept
mutants.rule: After a row with a regenerate step, every checkout file under its directory is the checkout's again: the next row's killers must not read this mutant's output.

mutants.name: rgk-any-row
mutants.rule: A build failure kills only a row with a regenerate step: the same failure of a named killer's suite with no step (names-renamed) is invalid.

mutants.name: rgk-detail-first-line
mutants.rule: A kill by a build failure after regenerate names the first compiler error, not the build's first line.

mutants.name: rgk-unnamed-killer
mutants.rule: A build failure after regenerate kills only through a suite of a killer the row names: a covering suite's failed build (regen-unnamed-build) is invalid.

mutants.name: regen-new-file-kept
mutants.rule: A file a regenerate step added that the checkout does not have is removed after the row.

mutants.name: regen-failure-ignored
mutants.rule: A regenerate step that fails makes the row invalid, as a mutated tree that does not build does; its output is the reason.

mutants.rule: A row's key holds every file its Go killers read.

mutants.name: gt2-whole-dropped
mutants.rule: A killer that is no Go package of the module keys the row on every source.

mutants.name: gt2-ignored-unkeyed
mutants.rule: A row's key holds the ignored files its Go killers read.

mutants.name: gt2-relative-root
mutants.rule: A relative -root still finds its packages' closures; else every row is keyed on every file.

mutants.name: gt6-ends-unchecked
